subject: Request: Exceptional Hosted API rate (28%) for ZenHealth — exec approval needed
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: ZenHealth — hostedapi ask: 28% rate concession (details & attachments)

Stephanie,

Quick context: ZenHealth (Series B digital-first payer) is ready to sign a 3-year committed hosted API contract if we can align on unit pricing. They’re proposing a ramp to ~3B tokens/mo by year 2. Procurement is pushing hard on list pricing + 40% off is their target; we negotiated them down to asking for 28% off our standard Hosted API list for committed volume.

Why this matters:
- Strategic market access into payer segment (case studies + potential co-marketing).
- Fast ramp projection with guaranteed minimums in SOW (see attached forecast + SOW).
- They’re willing to prepay Year 1, accept a 90-day onboarding SLA, and put our recommended security addenda in the SOW.

Request: need exec sign-off for a 28% concession on Hosted API unit rates (this exceeds 20% threshold and requires leadership approval). I put a recommended approval memo in the pricing_workbook and a short breakdown below.

Recommended commercial guardrails (if approved):
- 3-year term, committed minimum monthly spend $125k / month year 1 (escalating to $300k/mo by year 3)
- Prepayment: 6 months of year 1 fees upfront (refundable if contract fails to execute on our side)
- Technical: dedicated onboarding window, 48h priority triage for incidents during onboarding
- Legal: our standard terms + limited deviation in data retention and KMS integration (outlined in SOW)

Attachments: ZenHealth_SOW_v3.pdf, zenhealth_usage_forecast_q4-2027.xlsx, pricing_workbook_steph_v2.xlsx

TL;DR: big upside if we accept slightly deeper concession; downside controlled via term + prepayment. Please advise next steps / who to route to for final sign-off.

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ZenHealth — hostedapi ask: 28% rate concession (leadership approval needed)

Looping you both in — Ben put together the commercial and risk guardrails above. This is a >20% concession request for Hosted API (28% asked).

Mina — need finance perspective on margin impact and whether 28% with the proposed prepay & committed minimums is palatable. If you can’t sign off, what’s the absolute maximum you can support with finance controls?

Marissa — this is strategic in payer vertical. If you’re comfortable with the revenue profile and the marketing/partnership ask, can you provide an approval in thread or suggest alternate guardrails?

I’ve attached Ben’s pricing workbook and the SOW. My preference: approve conditionally if finance confirms breakeven margin at scale and legal signs off on the SOW redlines. Time sensitivity: ZenHealth needs final pricing by Friday 13 Aug to hit their board approval cycle.

Thanks — Steph
VP, Sales Operations
stephanie@redwood.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: ZenHealth — hostedapi ask: 28% rate concession (leadership approval needed)

Steph / Ben,

Reviewed the workbook and did a sensitivity on blended unit economics given their ramp profile. Short answer: 28% at list is aggressive but defensible under the proposed controls. Conditions from finance:

1) We accept up to 28% provided: a) 3-year committed term, b) minimum annual spend of $1.5M in Year 1 (we should lock MRR floors into SOW), c) 6-month prepayment applied against Year 1 committed minimum.
2) Include automatic uplift clauses if usage exceeds forecast by >20% (to protect margin).
3) Quarterly business reviews + usage gating for the first 6 months if error rates / abuse detected.

If Marissa confirms strategic value, I can sign off on finance side for 28% with those guardrails. Otherwise I can approve a 25% concession without the prepay requirement but with stronger audit clauses.

Marking this as Finance-sanctioned (conditional) pending legal review and your signoff Marissa.

—Mina
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: ZenHealth — hostedapi ask: 28% rate concession (leadership approval needed)

Team — thanks for the analysis. I agree with Mina’s conditions and recommend we approve the full 28% concession. Reasons:
- High strategic value: payer integration will unlock downstream opportunities across reference customers and partnerships (worth the initial unit margin tradeoff).
- Prepay + committed floors sufficiently mitigate near-term revenue risk.
- We should require a public joint case study and restrict the concession to Hosted API only (no embedding credits or transfer to other product lines).

Approval: Marissa Cole, SVP Revenue — APPROVE 28% conditional on: 1) Finance & Legal sign SOW redlines, 2) Marketing comms & co-case-study clause included, 3) Concession limited to Hosted API SKU and expires at contract renewal.

Ben — proceed to communicate to ZenHealth that we can accept 28% with listed guardrails and get Procurement to execute by Friday. Copy Legal on the redlines.

—Marissa
SVP, Revenue
marissa@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Avery Ross <avery@zenhealth.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@zenhealth.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ZenHealth — hostedapi ask: 28% rate concession (approval & next steps)

Avery — great to confirm: Redwood can approve a 28% concession on Hosted API unit pricing for the ZenHealth committed 3-year agreement. Conditions we discussed (and that will be reflected in the SOW):
- 3-year term with committed minimums (Year 1 minimum $1.5M annualized / 6 months prepaid),
- Concession applies to Hosted API SKU only, not embeddings or other add-ons,
- Quarterly business reviews and a usage uplift trigger to revisit pricing if you exceed forecast by >20%,
- Joint case study + comms window post-onboarding.

Next steps: I’ll send the updated SOW and DocuSign link for signatures by EOD. Legal will include the limited redlines we discussed. Please confirm by replying to this thread if Procurement is okay with the prepay cadence and committed minimum.

Thanks — excited to get ZenHealth live.

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
